outcomes: A TypeScript author binds an ordinary bun test to a declared check without changing how the test is written or what it returns
The verification wire receives what the runner observed, so a spec gate resolves TypeScript evidence exactly as it resolves Go and Python evidence
A repository that does not run the Putnami test adapter keeps its suite byte-for-byte unchanged
nonGoals: Deciding a verdict: the fragment states an observation and core recomputes every verdict against the authored criterion
Validating, attributing, or merging fragments — the test adapter owns all three
Supporting test runners other than bun

requirements.text: A bound test publishes exactly the verdict the runner observed and never alters that verdict: a settled body records passed, a throwing body records failed, a skipped test records skipped, and a body that never settles records nothing. One atomic fragment is written per check, carrying the declaring file and the test name as provenance.
Outside a Putnami-provided fragment directory the helpers register every test exactly as the bare runner would, write nothing, and cannot fail a run over reporting.

A fragment carries an acceptance verdict or a measurement, never both, so a producer can state a number but never its own verdict. A measuring body that threw or was skipped publishes nothing at all, and a published measurement carries the invocation window its body actually covered.
